{
  "hypothesis": "Predicted that line patterns with salient Gestalt information would elicit holistic processing comparable to that for human faces in novices without any training.",
  "design": "within-subjects design with factors Task (faces vs. line patterns), Alignment (aligned vs. misaligned), Congruency (congruent vs. incongruent), and Same/Different (same vs. different top parts).",
  "manipulation_or_predictor": "Presentation of composite faces versus composite line patterns possessing Gestalt information (connectedness, closure, and continuity), evaluated across aligned and misaligned stimulus configurations.",
  "outcome_measure": "Response sensitivity (d-prime) in same/different judgments of the top parts of composite stimuli.",
  "population_and_setting": "22 participants tested in a laboratory setting.",
  "sample_size_total": 22,
  "recruitment_and_incentive": "Not stated",
  "analysis_plan": "A repeated measures analysis of variance (ANOVA) examining main effects and interactions of alignment, congruency, and task, followed by tests of simple main effects and t-tests for congruency effects in aligned and misaligned conditions.",
  "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "not stated",
  "other_methods_notes": "Participants performed two composite tasks (one with faces and one with line patterns) with order counterbalanced across participants. Stimuli were presented sequentially with an intervening mask."
}
